newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end touch lower, market edgy.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end touch lower, market edgy.

text.p: Dutch shares closed an inch lower on Wednesday after modest recovery faded in the afternoon and dealers said investors remained nervous.
Weak dollar was among the factors that put a halt to a strong recovery in morning trade, with dealers already warned that another correction in the near-term was very possible.
Some dealers foresaw a correction of the AEX share index to 680 points. The AEX closed 0.05 points lower at 708.55 points.
Financials made a strong recovery in morning trade, since those stocks were the main victims during Tuesday's session, but most gains disappeared near the close.
Bank-insurer ING ended 0.20 guilders higher at 70.30, after touching 72.40 earlier.

Analysts expect ING's 1996 results tomorrow to be some 22 percent higher at 3.22 billion guilders. "There was quite some demand for ING call options," said one dealer, adding some were speculating on even better results.

The Midcap index only just managed to close higher as the index was off in late afternoon trade. Dealers said all share business was likely to remain volatile and they added that new U.S. data on Friday could give the market another stir.
Analysts expect a drop in U.S. March unemployment to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent in February.
Builder HBG was among the big gainers in the midcap. Food group CSM was also strong gaining 2.00 guilders to 104.50.
Copier maker Oce-van der Grinten made a modest rise, gaining 1.80 guilders to 235.80 and -- also in the AEX -- telecom group KPN added one guilder to 68.00 guilders.
Electronics firm Philips closed 0.30 guilders higher at 82.30. Polygram, majority owned by Philips, rose 1.20 guilders to 96.20 guilders.
